feed.title: Architecture & Building — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Arch2O
entry.summary: An architecture site giving competitions, software and learning content alongside project news. Unlike a pure project archive it also carries guides aimed at students and young architects.

entry.title: ArchDaily
entry.summary: The world’s largest architecture publication — daily projects, drawings and material news. Unlike Pinterest-style boards it presents each project with plans, sections and the architect’s statement.

entry.title: Archello
entry.summary: An architecture and design platform gathering projects, products and brands in one place.

entry.title: ArchEyes
entry.summary: An archive examining modern architecture classics in depth with drawings, plans and context.

entry.title: Archicad
entry.summary: An architect-focused BIM software rivalling Revit. Unlike Revit its interface is built around the architectural design flow — leaning to design more than engineering modules.

entry.title: Archinect
entry.summary: A long-running community site gathering architecture news, jobs and discussion.

entry.title: Architizer
entry.summary: A platform indexing architecture projects alongside building products. Unlike pure inspiration sites it also links the real products and manufacturers used in a project.

entry.title: Autodesk Revit
entry.summary: The industry standard for Building Information Modelling (BIM) — model, drawings and data in one file. Unlike pure drafting tools, a wall you place in plan updates automatically in section and the schedule.

entry.title: Designboom
entry.summary: A long-established online magazine covering architecture, design and art broadly.

entry.title: DETAIL
entry.summary: A reference magazine focused on construction detail and building solutions. Unlike inspiration sites it goes into “how it is built” — junctions, layers and material detail.

entry.title: Dezeen
entry.summary: A magazine covering architecture and design with a journalistic voice. Unlike ArchDaily’s project archive it leans on news, interviews and criticism.

entry.title: Divisare
entry.summary: An archive presenting architecture through photography alone, slow and selective. Unlike fast feeds it curates each project like a careful photo series.

entry.title: Domus
entry.summary: The archive of the authoritative Italian magazine on architecture and design, running since 1928.

entry.title: Enscape
entry.summary: A real-time visualisation tool embedded inside Revit, Rhino and SketchUp. Unlike separate render programs it gives a photorealistic view instantly while you design, with no export.

entry.title: MIT OCW · Mimarlık
entry.summary: The open courseware of MIT’s architecture department — from design studio to building technology. Unlike publication sites it gives the profession as an academic curriculum, course by course.

entry.title: Morphocode
entry.summary: Articles and tutorials teaching urban data, mapping and generative design.

entry.title: Parametric Architecture
entry.summary: A publication focused on parametric and computational design and AI in architecture.

entry.title: Pritzker Prize
entry.summary: The official site of the Pritzker Prize, architecture’s highest honour — laureates and citations. Unlike general lists it gives the field’s canon year by year, with the jury’s reasoning.

entry.title: Rhinoceros 3D
entry.summary: A free-form (NURBS) modelling tool; with the Grasshopper plugin, the hub of algorithmic design. Unlike box modellers it handles complex curved geometry and parametric setups.

entry.title: RIBA
entry.summary: The Royal Institute of British Architects’ site — professional standards, education and resources. Unlike publication sites it represents the institutional, official side of the profession.

entry.title: SketchUp
entry.summary: A fast 3D modelling tool for architecture and interiors. Unlike heavy CAD/BIM programs it is easy to learn — for turning an idea into massing in minutes.

entry.title: The Architectural Review
entry.summary: A long-standing British journal treating architecture with critical and theoretical depth.

entry.title: World-Architects
entry.summary: An international directory presenting profiles and projects of selected architects country by country.
